answer.rationale: Write-path p99 climbing for 90 min, onset shortly after a release 2h ago — temporal correlation makes the new build the leading suspect. memory_b1 supports rollback as a low-impact recovery for a release-correlated regression; memory_b6 would confirm whether gating should have caught this class of build. Read-replica routing (b5) targets read load, not the write path; failover (b2) and circuit breakers (b4) address dependency/regional faults with no evidence here; add_capacity (b3) fits forecastable surges, but settlement peak is daily and the timing coincides with the release. Rollback preserves customer writes (the prior stable build handled this traffic) and is reversible. Residual uncertainty: peak write volume could be a contributing factor, so post-rollback I will watch whether latency recovers; if not, capacity is the next window's action.
